name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.22.0 adds an optional data-rules stage: typed rules from a separate rule file are evaluated twice on one read-only PostgreSQL snapshot, as compiled SQL with bound parameters and as an independent standard-library Python evaluation, and a rule gets a verdict only when both agree and its authored examples hold. With views enabled, build creates lookup views whose rows data-rules certifies, so the keys a rule found are read in the database while results keep counts and ids only. Unsupported types, nondeterministic collations, NaN, NULL or duplicate keys, cycles and row budgets leave rules not_run, never passed. Configurations without data_rules keep byte-identical build output, results and reports apart from the engine fingerprint, and report never reads the data-rules result. Agreement of the two evaluations is not proof of the business rule. Earlier contract/plan report evidence, SQL structure diagnostics and synthetic fixtures are unchanged. Rerun operational stages after upgrading because engine code changed. Publication does not update active installations or company databases.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
